summary.tldr: Bans most replacement workers during lawful strikes or lockouts in federally regulated workplaces, and adds fines for breaking the rule.
what_it_does: Adds a rule that lets the Canada Industrial Relations Board settle a new collective agreement after 90 days of a strike or lockout, if the parties have bargained in good faith for at least 30 days and still have no agreement.
Requires employers to reinstate employees in the bargaining unit when a strike or lockout ends, ahead of other people.
Bars employers from using people hired during the notice-to-bargain period, contractors, other employees, or other outside help to do strikers' or locked-out workers' duties, except in limited cases.
Allows replacement workers only when needed to prevent danger to life, health or safety, major damage to equipment or premises, or serious environmental damage, and only for conservation purposes.
Lets the Minister appoint an investigator to check compliance, require assistance at the workplace, and order a report to the Minister and the parties.
Makes a person who breaks the replacement-worker rule guilty of an offence and liable to a fine of up to $100,000 for each day the offence continues.
summary.background: The bill changes parts of the Canada Labour Code that deal with strikes, lockouts, and collective bargaining.
